hints.title: Sorted Property and Space Optimization Obstacle
hints.text: A direct pair scan takes quadratic time and building an auxiliary lookup structure uses linear space. Given that the array is already sorted in non-decreasing order, how can you exploit the monotonic order using constant extra space?

hints.title: Monotonic Boundary Adjustment
hints.text: With numbers sorted, the sum of the smallest and largest available elements indicates how to adjust: if too small, increase the lower bound; if too large, decrease the upper bound.

hints.title: Two Pointers Converging Inward
hints.text: Place a pointer at index 0 and another at the end of the array. At each step, compute numbers[left] + numbers[right]. If the sum matches the target, return [left + 1, right + 1]. If the sum is less than target, increment left. If the sum is greater than target, decrement right.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of numbers array (2 <= N <= 3 * 10^4)
complexity.notes: Single pass converging inward with O(1) space, returning 1-indexed positions.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Exhaustive nested pair search takes O(N^2) time. Using a hash map achieves O(N) time but requires O(N) auxiliary memory, failing the constant extra space requirement.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Leveraging the sorted property allows converging inward with two pointers, achieving O(N) time with O(1) space instead of O(N) hash map memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Immediate convergence proof based on monotonicity, returning 1-indexed output as specified, and achieving O(1) auxiliary space.
